title: Model actors in the CLI and MCP

targets.text: culture-rules enrols each local model as its own actor from the gateways' /v1/models, lists where an actor is used, repoints a workflow from one actor to another and refuses to disable an actor still in use: one CLI verb and one MCP tool each, dry-run by default
culture-rules learn and the MCP tool list both show actors enrol-models, actors references and workflows repoint-actor, and actors disable carries the reference guard
The operator and the assisting agent who run culture-rules from the CLI or MCP and wire local models into workflows
The verbs are documented where the operator looks: explain catalog, learn, and docs/operations (a model-actors section)

Pointing a workflow step at a local model means hand-building actor JSON, editing the workflow JSON with its revision, and disabling the old actor: a multi-step script in the scratchpad (model-actors.sh, 2026-10-19), and actors update even needs a positional ID that the operator's first command missed
The scratchpad script model-actors.sh needed build/create/point/retire/check steps and hand-built JSON for one repoint (2026-10-19)

Three verb calls replace the script: actors enrol-models makes or updates one agent actor per matching model, workflows repoint-actor moves a workflow's steps to it with expected_revision, and actors disable refuses while an enabled workflow still names the actor; actors references shows where an actor is used
An end-to-end test against MemoryStore: enrol two models from a fake /v1/models, repoint a workflow, then actors disable on the old actor succeeds only after the repoint
Every lobes lane (cortex-spark, cortex-spark2, worker-thor, hand-spark2) becomes a ready actor any workflow can use, and moving work between lanes is a reviewed dry run instead of hand-edited JSON
One enrol-models run against the live lobes gateway with --match 'cortex-*' plans exactly cortex-spark and cortex-spark2, and nothing else

actors enrol-models takes repeatable --gateway MACHINE, each a key of the model_gateways variable (machine -> URL), in priority order, and --api-key grant:NAME (default grant:LOBES_GATEWAY_API_KEY); the server resolves the grant only after the gateway is found in model_gateways, GETs URL/v1/models, and the actor stores base_url = URL and params.api_key as the grant reference, never the value

A test asserts the bearer key is resolved on the server from the grant reference only, never appears in a response, --json output or the stored actor, and the stored params.api_key is the grant reference

Tests: --gateway with a name missing from model_gateways is refused with exit 1 naming the known gateways; a model_gateways entry change is picked up on the next call; the site's panel offers the model_gateways entries as its gateway choices

actors enrol-models enrols only models matching a repeatable --match glob (no default, so embedders, rerankers and Hugging Face names like unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 are never enrolled by accident); the actor id is the model id, and a model id that is not a valid actor id is refused
A test feeding the live model list (cortex-*, embedder-*, reranker-*, unsloth/...) plans only the --match hits, and a match with no valid id is refused with exit 1

Each enrolled actor is kind agent, on the gateway's MACHINE, with params base_url = URL, model = the model id, concurrency_pool from c3, max_concurrency 1; an existing actor with that id is updated only in those fields, a matching one is unchanged, and the plan shows create/update/unchanged per actor
Running enrol-models twice in a row plans 0 changes the second time; an actor edited by hand keeps every field outside the enrolled ones
actors references ID lists every workflow step (loop bodies included) whose action params.actor is ID, and every rule whose action names it, with workflow, step and enabled state; read-only
A test with a step inside a for_each body and a rule action naming the actor lists both

workflows repoint-actor WORKFLOW --from A --to B rewrites every params.actor == A in the workflow, loop bodies included, and PUTs with expected_revision; it refuses when B is missing, disabled or deleted, or when no step names A; it never edits description or notes, and lists steps whose notes mention A as warnings
Tests: a stale revision returns the 409 revision_conflict as a CliError; description and notes are byte-identical after a repoint; missing or disabled --to refuses with exit 1
actors disable ID refuses, in the dry run too, while an enabled workflow or rule still references the actor, naming them; --force disables anyway
A test: disable is refused while an enabled workflow references the actor, allowed once it is repointed, allowed with --force; a disabled workflow does not block

Each new verb follows the CLI contract (dry run by default, --apply, --json, exit 0/1/2, CliError, explain catalog entry and learn mention) as a thin wrapper over its endpoint; MCP gets each as a tool through the registry, and the parity test covers them
tests/test_mcp_parity (or its equivalent) passes with the new verbs, and uv run teken cli doctor . --strict stays green

The logic lives in the server, so the CLI, MCP and site share one implementation: POST /actors/enrol-models (dry_run plan, then apply), GET /actors/{id}/references, POST /workflows/{id}/repoint-actor (dry_run, expected_revision), and POST /actors/{id}/disable refusing 409 actor_in_use unless force; api/openapi.json pins them, and a server + node rollout ships them
tests/server/test_openapi_contract.py passes with the four endpoints pinned in api/openapi.json, and the web client's types compile against them

The committed newspaper bundle (docs/rules/newspaper) moves its summary step to cortex-spark2 and drops actors/newspaper-llm.json for a cortex-spark2 actor; docs/operations/newspaper.md and the bundle tests follow
tests/rules/test_newspaper_bundle.py and test_newspaper_flow.py pass with the bundle on cortex-spark2, and grep finds no newspaper-llm under docs/rules

On the live store, 3 commands with no hand-written JSON (enrol-models, repoint-actor daily-newspaper, actors disable newspaper-llm) leave daily-newspaper's 1 llm.complete step on cortex-spark2, and the next 05:00 issue has 4 of 4 section summaries written by cortex-spark2
The 3 live commands are recorded with their output, and the next issue's run record shows the summary step's actor as cortex-spark2 with 4 summaries

The Actors page gains: an 'Add models from a gateway' panel (gateways, match, pool overrides; shows the server's plan, then applies), a 'Used by' list on an actor (from references, linking each workflow), a 'Move to another actor' action on that list (repoint, with the revision-conflict Reload), and Disable showing the in-use refusal with the workflows named
vitest and Playwright cover the panel's plan-then-apply, the Used by list, a repoint with a stale revision showing Reload, and the refused Disable; the webglass agent-state gate stays green
Screenshots of the Add models panel, the Used by list, the Move action and the refused Disable, in light and dark, are sent to the operator and approved before merge
No change to the engine or to any action kind, except one added refusal in llm.complete (model_taken, c26); the new endpoints only read and write actors and workflows through the store
git diff main under culture_rules/node and culture_rules/engine shows only the model_taken check in node/actions/llm.py and its tests

One enabled actor per model: creating or updating an enabled agent actor, or enabling one, whose params.model is already held by another enabled agent actor is refused (409 model_taken, naming the holder and saying to disable it first) in POST/PUT /actors, POST /actors/{id}/enable and enrol-models' plan; a disabled actor holds nothing; at runtime llm.complete refuses a step whose actor's model is also held by another enabled actor (model_taken)

Tests: create, update and enable of a second enabled actor for cortex-spark2 each return 409 model_taken naming the holder; the same actor created disabled is allowed and enables once the holder is disabled; enrol-models plans the refusal; a store seeded with two enabled holders makes llm.complete fail with model_taken

enrol-models never sends a resolved secret to an arbitrary URL: it is admin-only (culture_rules/auth/policy.py defaults an unmatched POST to admin; keep it off _EDITOR_PATTERNS), and each --gateway must name an entry in an allow-listed set of model gateways rather than a free URL, so an editor cannot point the server, with grant:ANY_SECRET, at a host they control

Tests: an editor-role call to POST /actors/enrol-models is 403; a gateway URL outside the allowlist is refused before any secret is resolved (the resolver is never called); the bearer header is only ever sent to an allow-listed host

The one-enabled-actor-per-model rule (c26) covers only endpoint actors, those whose params carry base_url (the llm.complete shape); bridge agents with a harness (qwen-fixer and qwen-reviewer both hold model cortex, enabled, live) are outside it, so the rule never refuses an edit to them

A test with qwen-fixer and qwen-reviewer from the live actors snapshot (same model cortex, no base_url, both enabled) lets PUT and enable on either succeed; the live store passes a dry check of the rule before rollout (0 conflicts besides newspaper-llm)

actors references and the disable guard also count placement.actor on steps and rules (culture_rules/model/placement.py: a step or rule placed on an actor runs on its machine); repoint-actor rewrites only action params.actor and reports placement references to A as warnings, never moving where a step runs
A test: a step placed on actor A shows in references with kind placement, blocks disable, and is listed but unchanged by repoint-actor

repoint-actor on a workflow whose v1 or v2 digest is in the trusted set warns in the dry run that the repoint drops its trust (culture_rules/actors/trusted.py: workflow_digest_v2 keeps step params, so a changed params.actor changes the digest), and refuses without --force
A test: repointing a trusted workflow fixture is refused without --force with the digest named, and with --force the new digest is shown so a trust update can follow

Version skew fails clearly: a new CLI against a server without the endpoints exits 2 with a 'server too old, needs culture-rules >= the new version' hint (as rollout's no_rollouts_endpoints does), and the site hides the new controls when the endpoints answer 404
A test: each new verb against a 404 endpoint raises CliError exit 2 with the version hint; the web test with the endpoint mocked 404 shows no Add models panel

Every write the new endpoints make goes through the server's Lifecycle (audit with the caller), one audit entry per actor created or updated and per workflow repointed, and the response lists the resulting ids and revisions
A test reads the audit log after an enrol-models apply and a repoint and finds one entry per change naming the caller
enrol-models refuses (in the plan) a model whose id is already the id of a non-agent actor or of an agent actor without base_url, rather than overwriting it into an endpoint actor
A test: a model id equal to an existing app actor's id plans a refusal and leaves the actor byte-identical

acceptance_criteria: plan_model_enrolment(existing, gateways, match, pools, api_key) plans create/update/unchanged/refused per model from gateways given as ordered (machine, url, model ids); tests/actors/test_model_enrol.py feeds the live model list (cortex-*, embedder-*, reranker-*, unsloth/...) and plans only --match hits
the first gateway listed wins and later ones appear as also_served_by; models an existing endpoint actor holds but no gateway lists are reported as unseen, never disabled

pool defaults to the model id with model=pool overrides; an update touches only kind-agnostic enrolled fields (machine, params.base_url, params.model, params.concurrency_pool, params.max_concurrency, params.api_key); a second run over the result plans 0 changes
an invalid actor id, or an id held by a non-agent actor or an agent actor without base_url, plans a refusal and the existing doc is untouched
tasks.instruction: Model it on culture_rules/actors/enrol_agents.py (Plan, change records, plan_enrolment). No I/O: the caller passes the model lists. Reuse the actor id validation the model layer applies. Zero third-party imports.

tasks.summary: Actor references and repoint (pure, stdlib): culture_rules/actors/references.py
acceptance_criteria: find_references(actor_id, workflows, rules) returns {workflow|rule, id, step path, via: action|placement, enabled}, walking for_each bodies at any depth; tests/actors/test_references.py covers a loop-body step, a rule action and a placed step

repoint_workflow(doc, frm, to) returns (new_doc, changed step paths, warnings): it rewrites only config.action.params.actor == frm, leaves description and notes byte-identical, and warns for notes that mention frm and for placement.actor == frm (unchanged)
repoint_workflow with no matching step raises a typed error the server maps to 409/422
tasks.instruction: Step shape: docs/rules/newspaper/workflows/daily-newspaper.json (summarise.body[summary].config.action.params.actor). Placement: culture_rules/model/placement.py. Rules' actions carry params.actor too. Work on plain dicts; return new dicts (copy.deepcopy), never mutate the input.

acceptance_criteria: is_endpoint_actor(doc) is true only for kind agent with a non-empty params.base_url; model_holder(actors, candidate) returns the id of another enabled, non-deleted endpoint actor with the same params.model, else None

tests/actors/test_model_rule.py uses the live snapshot shapes: qwen-fixer and qwen-reviewer (model cortex, no base_url, enabled) never conflict; newspaper-llm vs a new cortex-spark2 does; a disabled holder holds nothing
tasks.instruction: One small module both the server guards and node/actions/llm.py import, so the rule has one definition.

tasks.summary: Server routes: POST /actors/enrol-models, GET /actors/{id}/references, POST /workflows/{id}/repoint-actor in culture_rules/server/model_actors.py, registered from app.py
acceptance_criteria: enrol-models takes {gateways: [machine...], match, pools, api_key, dry_run}; each gateway is looked up in the model_gateways variable first, an unknown one is refused with the known names, and the grant resolver is called only after that (a test asserts the resolver and transport are never called on refusal)

/v1/models is read through an injectable transport (like discord_transport) with the resolved bearer; the key never appears in a response or the stored actor; tests/server/test_model_actors_api.py covers dry run, apply and model_gateways changes taking effect on the next call

repoint-actor takes {from, to, expected_revision, force, dry_run}: a stale revision is 409 revision_conflict, a missing/disabled/deleted target or no match is refused, a workflow whose v1 or v2 digest is trusted (culture_rules/actors/trusted.py) is refused without force naming the digest, and with force the new digest is returned
every write goes through Lifecycle (one audit entry per actor created/updated and per workflow repointed, naming the caller); responses list ids and revisions
tasks.instruction: Follow _register_discord_targets (app.py:975) for the resolver/transport injection; add one _register_model_actors(...) line in create_app. Reads of model_gateways use the Variables store. Keep the logic in t1/t2's modules; this file is routing, auth context and I/O.

tasks.summary: Actor guards on the definition routes: model_taken on create/update/enable, actor_in_use on disable (culture_rules/server/actor_guards.py, called from _register_kind)
acceptance_criteria: POST /actors, PUT /actors/{id} and POST /actors/{id}/enable return 409 model_taken naming the holder and saying to disable it first when model_holder finds one; creating the actor disabled is allowed and it enables once the holder is disabled

POST /actors/{id}/disable returns 409 actor_in_use listing the enabled workflows and rules that reference it (action or placement), disabled ones not counting; ?force=true disables anyway; tests/server/test_actor_guards_api.py covers each
existing tests in tests/server (test_api.py, test_authz_matrix.py) still pass unchanged
tasks.instruction: Guards live in the server layer, not culture_rules/engine (boundary c23). Hook them in _register_kind only for kind == 'actors'. Depends on t4 only because both touch app.py; land after it.

acceptance_criteria: llm.complete fails the step with 'model_taken: <holder>' when another enabled endpoint actor holds its actor's model; tests/node (llm action tests) seed two holders in MemoryStore and assert the failure, and the existing llm tests pass unchanged
git diff main touches culture_rules/node only in node/actions/llm.py and culture_rules/engine not at all
tasks.instruction: Import model_holder from culture_rules/actors/model_rule.py. Check after load_bound_actor and before the HTTP call; the failure string follows the module's '<code>: <detail>' convention.

tasks.summary: Newspaper bundle on cortex-spark2 (docs/rules/newspaper, docs/operations/newspaper.md, bundle tests)
acceptance_criteria: docs/rules/newspaper/actors/newspaper-llm.json is replaced by actors/cortex-spark2.json (agent, machine spark, base_url http://127.0.0.1:8001, model cortex-spark2, pool qwen-spark2, max_concurrency 1, api_key grant:LOBES_GATEWAY_API_KEY), and the summary step's params.actor is cortex-spark2
tests/rules/test_newspaper_bundle.py, test_newspaper_flow.py and the describe fixtures pass; grep -r newspaper-llm docs/rules returns nothing; docs/operations/newspaper.md names cortex-spark2
tasks.instruction: Only actor names and the technical notes field change; never edit description prose. Check scripts/scan-secrets.py still passes (loopback URL only).

tasks.summary: Pin the contract and roles: api/openapi.json, culture_rules/auth/policy.py, tests/server/test_authz_matrix.py
acceptance_criteria: api/openapi.json carries the three new routes and the disable force parameter; tests/server/test_openapi_contract.py passes
the route matrix makes POST /actors/enrol-models admin (an editor gets 403), GET /actors/{id}/references viewer, POST /workflows/{id}/repoint-actor editor; test_authz_matrix.py asserts all three
tasks.instruction: Regenerate the pinned schema the way the repo does it (see the contract test for the command); never hand-edit the paths. Policy: leave enrol-models out of _EDITOR_PATTERNS so it defaults to admin.

tasks.summary: CLI verbs and MCP tools: actors enrol-models, actors references, actors disable --force, workflows repoint-actor (cli/_commands/actors.py, workflows.py, explain/catalog.py, learn)
acceptance_criteria: each verb is dry-run by default, --apply commits, --json works, errors are CliError with exit 1 (user) or 2 (environment); actors enrol-models takes repeatable --gateway, --match, --pool model=pool and --api-key
against a server that 404s the new routes each verb exits 2 with a 'server too old: needs culture-rules >= <version>' hint (as rollout's no_rollouts_endpoints)
explain catalog entries and a learn mention exist; the MCP parity test lists the four tools; uv run teken cli doctor . --strict is green
tasks.instruction: Thin wrappers over the t4/t5 endpoints via ctx.client.request; reuse _nounlib.write for dry-run/apply envelopes. actors disable keeps its positional ID and gains --force.

tasks.summary: Actors page: Add models from a gateway, Used by, Move to another actor, in-use Disable (web/src/actors, web/src/api/actors.ts)
acceptance_criteria: the Add models panel offers the model_gateways entries, takes match and pool overrides, shows the server's dry-run plan, then applies; an actor shows Used by (references, each linking its workflow) with a Move action that repoints and shows Reload on a stale revision; Disable shows the in-use refusal naming the workflows
the controls are hidden when the endpoints 404; vitest and Playwright cover each flow; typecheck, the webglass agent-state gate and the web CI job pass
screenshots of the four states in light and dark are sent to the operator and approved before merge
tasks.instruction: Existing Actors board style (ActorsBoard.tsx, ActorForm.tsx, actors.css); large targets, keyboard access, prefers-reduced-motion. Types come from api/openapi.json.

tasks.summary: Docs, harness files and version: docs/operations/model-actors.md, CLAUDE.md + QWEN.md + AGENTS.override.md + AGENTS.colleague.md in step, minor bump, end-to-end test
acceptance_criteria: docs/operations/model-actors.md covers model_gateways, the three verbs, the model rule and the one-time newspaper move; the four harness prompt files describe the verbs consistently; markdownlint and harness-smoke pass
tests/test_model_actors_e2e.py (MemoryStore): enrol two models from a fake /v1/models, repoint a workflow, and actors disable on the old actor succeeds only after the repoint
version-bump minor (pyproject.toml, CHANGELOG.md) and uv.lock updated; the full suite and lint pass
tasks.instruction: Use the version-bump skill. Load-bearing phrases in the harness files stay (see CLAUDE.md, Identity and the four harnesses).

tasks.summary: Live: model_gateways variable, rollout, the three commands, evidence
acceptance_criteria: after the PR merges and the rollout verifies, the operator runs: variables set model_gateways {spark: http://127.0.0.1:8001}, actors disable newspaper-llm --force, actors enrol-models --gateway spark --match 'cortex-*' --pool cortex-spark2=qwen-spark2 (dry run plans exactly cortex-spark and cortex-spark2), workflows repoint-actor daily-newspaper --from newspaper-llm --to cortex-spark2; outputs recorded as evidence
the next 05:00 issue's run record shows the summary step on cortex-spark2 with 4 of 4 summaries; the before-state evidence is the scratchpad model-actors.sh (5 steps, hand-built JSON)
tasks.instruction: Deploys and shared-resource writes go through the operator's shell (offer a step script); the admin token is injected with grant run --inject, never read.

risks.text: The guards live in the server routes (boundary c23 keeps them out of culture_rules/engine), so writes that bypass the API (rollout import's store path, migrations, the node) skip model_taken/actor_in_use; the llm.complete runtime check (t6) is the backstop
Mixed-version window during the rollout: nodes not yet on the new version skip the runtime check, and the old site lacks the controls; run the live commands (t12) only after rollout verify
Concurrent creates or enables for one model and a repoint racing a disable stay check-then-write (frame parks v1, v2); no unique index is added
